messages:
triage-bot: [ALERT] Lotus (private-vpc: prod-dedicated) egress error rate spike -> 5xx from external API (thirdparty-payments). Severity: P1. Pager: oncall-sre-Anna. Links: https://incidents.redwood.example/1756004321

oncall-sre-Anna: acknowledged, joining. oncall handoff in 5m if no resolution.

netops-Miguel: seeing NLB target group marked unhealthy in eu-west-1a only. Health checks failing with TCP RST from targets. Logs show security-group reject for outbound 443 to 52.16.0.0/12 (thirdparty IP range).

eng-runtime-Li: curious — Lotus is on a dedicated private pool with tenant isolation, but egress uses customer-managed NAT gateway. Any NAT exhaustion?

se-Devon: Customer note: Lotus uses a heavy payment connector to thirdparty-payments with a persistent pool of sockets. They have reserved capacity on Dedicated but still hit external rate limits. Customer reported timeouts ~10:40 UTC.

netops-Miguel: quick checks:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:eu-west-1:...
# returns Unhealthy 1/3 targets (eu-west-1a) status: connection refused / reset
sudo iptables -t nat -L -n | grep 10.0.0.0/16 || true
# NAT conntrack utilization: 85% on nat-01-lotus
```

oncall-sre-Anna: possible causes: SG change at tenant level, NAT conntrack exhaustion, or thirdparty blacklisting. We need to isolate cause quickly. Miguel, can you confirm any recent SG changes?

netops-Miguel: I see a security group rule change at 10:35 UTC: outbound rule tightened to only allow 10.11.0.0/16 -> 0.0.0.0/0 removed by automation. That would break egress to 52.16.0.0/12. Change was rolled by infra-autoscale-policy. Rolling back now as emergency.

security-Jess: rollback approved. Adding temporary allow:
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-egress --group-id sg-0lotus --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 52.16.0.0/12
```

eng-runtime-Li: while SG is reverting, suggest we also shift traffic off eu-west-1a targets to eu-west-1b/c for the NLB. We can update target group weights (drain 1a) and reduce healthcheck aggressiveness to avoid flapping.

se-Devon: customer authorization for a short TTL DNS weight shift? Rakesh, can you confirm customer ok to move traffic to another AZ for mitigation? This may route via a different NAT they own.

cust-su-Rakesh: confirmed, Lotus approves temporary AZ shift and DNS weight change. They want a blameless postmortem. Please keep them updated every 10m.

netops-Miguel: executing weight shift:
```
# mark targets in 1a draining
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d
# adjust route 53 weighted record to 0.2 for eu-west-1a -> 0.0, 0.8 split to other AZs
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://weight-shift.json
```

triage-bot: Incident comment added. Customer impact: payment connector timeouts for ~30% of requests from eu-west-1a clients. Ticket created: INC-1756004321.

oncall-sre-Anna: SG rollback completed at 10:48 UTC, new egress allow in place. Netops, what's conntrack after rollback?

netops-Miguel: conntrack calibrated down to 45% after temporary NAT restart on nat-01-lotus. Healthchecks returning healthy now for NLB targets in 1a.

eng-runtime-Li: rolling restart of runtime worker group in Lotus dedicated pool scheduled to clear stale sockets (graceful). Command: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/lotus-runtime -n lotus-prod` — doing now.

se-Devon: customer notified: "We applied temporary network rule rollback and shifted traffic to other AZs, you should see reduced errors. We're on it with root cause." Rakesh will escalate to their infra team to check for client-side rate limiting tokens.

cust-su-Rakesh: Lotus confirms reduced error rates to baseline. They saw a short window of failed payments but no data loss. Requesting timeline and detection details.

security-Jess: adding follow-up actions: pin automation to require two-step approval before tightening egress rules for customers with private NATs; add guardrail to not remove 0.0.0.0/0 outbound unless explicit.

triage-bot: Status -> mitigated (P1->P2) at 10:58 UTC. Next: postmortem draft owner: oncall-sre-Anna. Customer follow-up: cust-su-Rakesh. RCA due in 72 hours.

oncall-sre-Anna: tagging handoff — I'll continue as incident lead until 11:30 UTC then rotate to oncall-sre-Jordan. Please drop notes in the incident doc.

eng-runtime-Li: adding perf note — dedicated pool had high socket churn; consider increasing ephemeral port range and enabling TCP keepalive tuning for Lotus workloads.

netops-Miguel: also recommend conntrack limit bump for nat-01-lotus to 200k (currently 65k) and to monitor for NAT exhaustion alerts.

cust-su-Rakesh: customer requested a short summary to send to their SRE: "Redwood rolled back restrictive egress SG rule that blocked third-party endpoints and shifted traffic away from affected AZ; services recovered. RCA and remediation plan forthcoming."

oncall-sre-Anna: confirmed. Closing thread for active mitigation; will post final postmortem link when ready. :white_check_mark:
